messages:
matt: quick check — thinking about moving per-model runtime config out of a single ConfigMap into a CRD + operator so we can 1) avoid giant CM reconciles, 2) have per-model ownership + validation, and 3) support hot reload per-pod via annotation. thoughts?

liz: +1 on idea. can you sketch the migration path? worried about TF and helm changes for prod clusters. :eyes:

matt: rough plan: create a ModelConfig CRD (namespaced). operator watches ModelConfig and writes a small config file into an emptyDir mounted at /etc/model-config/<model>. When operator updates file, we touch a checksum annotation on the PodSpec to trigger rollout. This avoids stuffing everything in one CM.

olga: how do we handle secrets (api keys, license blobs)? currently some models reference secrets via envFrom.

matt: two options: 1) operator can reference k8s Secret refs and project-inject to the pod as env or projected volume (requires RBAC), or 2) keep secrets in Secret objects and ModelConfig only has references (safer). leaning to #2.

kevin: TF impact: need CRD install (helm or kustomize) + RBAC binding for operator service account. Also update infra module that creates ConfigMap per-environment to stop writing per-model keys. I'll open a TF RFC.

ryan: runtime concerns: how will we ensure kernel picks up new KV cache config without restarting workers? hot reload currently looks at CONFIGMAP_CHECKSUM annotation in deployment to restart. If operator does file write inside pod, runtime won't necessarily re-read unless we implement an inotify watcher in the runtime or use sidecar to signal.

matt: good point. two approaches: add a tiny sidecar that watches file and posts `POST /-/reload` to runtime admin port; or operator can patch the deployment annotation (CONFIG_CHECKSUM) to force rollout. sidecar is nicer for zero-downtime reloads but adds complexity.

liz: prefer patching annotation for initial MVP — fewer moving parts and we already have the rollout machinery. Sidecar for smoother rollover can be follow-up.

olga: for the TF PR, can we ensure the CRD is deployed only after the operator service account exists? ordering in modules tends to be annoying.

kevin: yes, in the infra module I can add a `kubernetes_manifest.crd` resource and make the operator helm release depend_on the service account resource. will share snippet in PR.

matt: example ModelConfig YAML (WIP):
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood.ai/v1
kind: ModelConfig
metadata:
  name: llama-7b
  namespace: prod-models
spec:
  modelRef: s3://models/llama-7b/sha123
  runtimeFlags:
    max_tokens: 2048
    sampling: "top_k"
  secretRefs:
    - name: llama-license
      key: license.pem
```

ryan: looks good. one ask: include `reloadStrategy: annotation|sidecar` in spec so operator can choose behavior per-model.

matt: added in my head. :grin:

ci-bot: matt requested review of branch `feature/model-config-crd` — https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/421 :github: (status: checks running)

deploy-bot: prod cluster: helm release `model-config-operator` pending upgrade (namespace: infra-operators)

liz: can someone run a quick smoke test in staging? specifically: create ModelConfig -> operator writes file -> operator patches deployment annotation -> one deployment pod restarts and picks up new flags.

olga: I'll run it after lunch, ping me with the staging namespace.

kevin: Terraform notes for PR:
```
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "modelconfig_crd" {
  manifest = file("crds/modelconfig.yaml")
}

resource "helm_release" "model_config_operator" {
  name       = "model-config-operator"
  repository = "https://charts.redwood.ai/ops"
  chart      = "model-config-operator"
  depends_on = [kubernetes_service_account.operator_sa, kubernetes_manifest.modelconfig_crd]
}
```

matt: perf/scale thought: in prod we may have thousands of ModelConfig CRs. CRD list operations are heavy; operator should shard using label selectors and have per-shard workers. also watch for API server QPS.

ryan: yep enforce rate-limits on the controller and add an informers-based cache. also add a prom counter for reconcile durations.

liz: for rollout plan: 1) deploy CRD + operator in staging, 2) migrate 2-3 low-traffic models to CRD (manual), 3) monitor CPU of kube-apiserver and operator, 4) flip infra module to stop writing big ConfigMap, 5) bulk migrate remaining models with canary waves.

matt: leaving action items:
- kevin: open TF PR and include helm depends_on + RBAC (ETA tomorrow)
- olga: smoke test in staging (today after lunch)
- ryan: add reloadStrategy flag to runtime admin doc and a tiny inotify proof-of-concept (ETA 48h)
- liz: draft migration runbook and rollback steps (ETA EOD)

liz: sounds good. tagging @olga @kevin @ryan on the tasks. :thumbsup:

olga: staging namespace is `staging-models` — I'll post logs after test.

ci-bot: checks passed for PR 421 — all green :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: `model-config-operator` upgraded to v0.1.0 in staging (infra-operators) — rollout 3/3 pods ready

olga: smoke test results: created ModelConfig for `test-llama-small`, operator created file at `/etc/model-config/test-llama-small/config.json`, deployment annotation patched `config-checksum: b5a3f2`, one pod restarted and logs show new flag `max_tokens=512` applied. no errors. attaching snippet:
```
2026-09-14T12:43:02Z operator INFO wrote /etc/model-config/test-llama-small/config.json
2026-09-14T12:43:05Z operator INFO patched deployment apps/v1/test-llama-small config-checksum=b5a3f2
2026-09-14T12:43:20Z runtime INFO loaded model config from /etc/model-config/test-llama-small/config.json
```

matt: awesome, thanks olga. I'll start the design doc for operator sharding.

liz: great progress — we'll discuss in sync tomorrow. closing this thread for now, ping here if anything breaks. :lock:
